entries.25fc0f363a3be985: The company makes measuring instruments that check communication speed and quality, inspection equipment that checks weight and foreign matter at food plants, and test equipment for EV batteries and drive systems. The annual securities report says the information and communications market, the main market of the Telecommunications Measurement Business, has fast technological innovation, so products and parts tend to become obsolete, and that the company works to secure a stable supply of electronic components and other parts.
entries.299587f075bca2ca: Automobile manufacturers, automotive parts manufacturers and battery manufacturers (the counterparties that the securities report's [Business Risks] section describes as having a high share of sales of EV and battery test equipment)
entries.2cfc13f64df21158: Operating profit for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥14,828 million (up 22.3%), profit before tax was ¥16,147 million (up 26.8%), and profit attributable to owners of the parent was ¥11,677 million (up 26.1%). The annual securities report states that profitability of the Communications Measurement Business improved through reduced inventories and cost control. Segment operating profit was ¥10,782 million for the Communications Measurement Business, ¥3,318 million for the PQA Business, ¥850 million for the Environmental Measurement Business and ¥1,972 million for Other.

entries.3075cc2786d42fbe: Businesses including sensing and devices, logistics, welfare services and real estate leasing. Because the securities report describes this category as business segments and the like not included in the reportable segments, it is placed last regardless of the size of its revenue. Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥6,867 million (up 12.9% year on year), and operating profit was ¥1,972 million (up 35.4%). Subsidiaries including Anritsu Devices Co., Ltd., Anritsu Kosan Co., Ltd. and Anritsu Real Estate Co., Ltd. handle the manufacture of the Company's products, logistics services, real estate leasing and similar activities.
entries.31fdc7632cce1800: The company, 51 subsidiaries and 2 affiliates develop, manufacture and sell measuring instruments, quality inspection equipment and others, and also provide maintenance and services. Consolidated headcount is 4,114 employees (as of March 31, 2026; the average number of temporary employees for the year was 540). R&D investment (including development costs recorded as intangible assets) was ¥10,179 million in the fiscal year ended March 2026, or 8.7% of net sales.
entries.375244be2c25c660: Takasago Seisakusho Co., Ltd. remains a wholly owned (100%) subsidiary as of March 31, 2026, and belongs to the Environmental Measurement Business. The securities report states that it has strengths in power supply systems that use advanced energy control technology, and that it provides test equipment for EV drive systems and batteries.
entries.39e96c06f7efa3fd: This is a reporting segment that makes and sells production management and quality assurance equipment and systems used in factories for food, pharmaceuticals, and cosmetics, such as automatic checkweighers, automatic electronic weighing machines, foreign object detectors, and integrated quality management and control systems (the annual securities report notes that PQA is an abbreviation for Products Quality Assurance). In the fiscal year ended March 2026, revenue was ¥31,033 million (up 9.9% from the previous fiscal year), accounting for 26% of consolidated revenue, and operating profit was ¥3,318 million (up 17.0%). Anritsu Infivis Co., Ltd. manufactures the company's products, and subsidiaries in the United States, the Netherlands, China, and Thailand handle sales and manufacturing. The annual securities report states that revenue and profit increased due to investment demand for automation and labor saving in quality assurance in the food market, the launch of new products in Japan, expansion of production capacity by food manufacturers driven by inbound demand, and replacement demand for automatic checkweighers resulting from revisions to the measurement system. The overseas sales ratio is about 5-tenths.
entries.3aab41af5e96687c: A measuring instrument manufacturer based in Atsugi, Kanagawa Prefecture, that makes and sells mainly electronic measuring instruments for telecommunications, as well as inspection equipment for food factories and testing equipment for EVs.

entries.45b96a6ba7138bfa: A reportable segment that makes and sells test equipment for EVs and batteries, power measuring instruments and data acquisition systems, and monitoring solutions for video surveillance of roads, dams, rivers and similar sites. Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥10,787 million (up 26.2% year on year), accounting for 9% of consolidated revenue, and operating profit was ¥850 million (down 5.5%). Takasago, Ltd. provides test equipment for EV drivetrains and batteries, drawing on its strength in power supply systems, and DEWETRON GmbH of Austria, all of whose shares were acquired on October 21, 2025, has been included in the scope of consolidation since November, during the third quarter. The securities report states that revenue increased because DEWETRON GmbH was consolidated, while profit decreased because, in demand for EV and battery testing in Japan, customer investment was delayed against the background of U.S. tariff policy and an adjustment phase in EV investment.
entries.46fa007c143ee9d6: A reportable segment that makes and sells measuring instruments for digital communications and IP networks, for optical communications, for mobile communications, and general-purpose RF, microwave and millimeter-wave measuring instruments, as well as service assurance. Of the 3 reportable segments, it has the largest revenue from external customers. Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥68,774 million (down 1.9% year on year), accounting for 59% of consolidated revenue, and operating profit was ¥10,782 million (up 28.7%). The securities report states that this business is divided into 3 sub-segments serving the "network infrastructure market," the "mobile market" and the "electronics market." In addition to the Company's own manufacturing and sales, Tohoku Anritsu Co., Ltd. manufactures the Company's products, and sales subsidiaries in the United States, Europe, Asia and elsewhere sell and maintain the Company's products. The securities report states that customer investment, which had been delayed by U.S. tariff policy, recovered and demand related to data centers was strong, but revenue fell because the first-quarter decline could not be recovered, while profitability improved through reduced inventories and cost control.
